Subject: Post-demo: Acme Health security discovery & roadmap next steps

Hi Dominic —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps to keep momentum on compliance evaluation: 

Key takeaways
- Acme Health is evaluating Redwood for patient-facing summarization and internal knowledge search; HIPAA is a hard requirement.
- Primary concerns: SOC 2 Type II reports, SOC scope (production vs. non-prod), GDPR/data residency, and FedRAMP/BAA expectations for PHI handling.
- Procurement timeline: target decision Q3 2026; security review must complete before procurement sign-off.

Immediate asks (from Acme team)
1) Please share the latest SOC 2 Type II report and our vendor security questionnaire template (attachment requested).
2) Clarify whether Redwood operates a HIPAA-ready offering and whether we provide a BAA for Private/Dedicated customers.
3) High-level roadmap for ISO 27001 and FedRAMP ambitions and timing.

Proposed Redwood next steps
- I attached the vendor questionnaire template we use for security reviews (vendor_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx). Could you fill and return within two weeks?
- I'll share the public SOC 2 package (SOC2-TypeII-Report-2024.pdf) and a short note on our HIPAA posture.
- Internally, I’ll loop Legal and Security to scope SOC coverage and timeline for ISO/FedRAMP planning.

Would Monday 4/13 10am PT work for a short sync with Dominic + security?

Thanks,
Rishi
--

Rishi —

Appreciate the clear recap. Short answers and notes: 

- We’ll complete the vendor questionnaire; I assigned it to our security analyst (Ana) and procurement. Expect a first pass by 4/25.
- Yes, HIPAA compliance is mandatory. We will need a copy of Redwood's BAA and confirmation that PHI can be processed under Private/Dedicated configurations.
- SOC 2: we will need the latest Type II and evidence that the report covers production systems that would process PHI. If SOC 2 covers only non-prod, that will be a blocker.
- ISO 27001 and FedRAMP: these are ‘nice to haves’ for us (ISO more important). FedRAMP is a multi-year program — we won’t require FedRAMP for initial contract, but we will ask for roadmap and commitment.

We can do Mon 4/13 10am PT. I’ll invite Ana from security.

Thanks,
Dominic

Rishi / team —

I reviewed Dominic's points and attached a short BAA template and a suggested SOC scoping memo (attached as iso27001-prelim-roadmap.pdf and SOC2-scope-notes.txt). High-level notes: 

- BAA: We can provide a standard BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments with limited redlines. For Hosted customers, BAA is supported under our Dedicated offering only — we should state that upfront.
- SOC 2 scope: Current Type II report covers production inference and control plane for our hosted offering; Dedicated customers can be included under a SOC addendum (timeline: 3-4 months for inclusion in scope for baseline controls). If Acme requires SOC evidence that explicitly names their dedicated instance, that moves to a committed SOC scoping engagement.
- ISO 27001: We are beginning a gap assessment in Q2 2026; target certification start in late 2026 with expected certification in H2 2027 (depends on remediation). This is sufficient for Acme's procurement signal.
- FedRAMP: Long-term; we should present it as multi-year with milestones (assessment -> readiness -> provisional authorization). Not a blocker for initial contract but include as roadmap item.

Ask: Rishi, please send the SOC2-TypeII-Report-2024.pdf and the vendor questionnaire to Dominic and Ana before the 10am PT sync. I'll bring a BAA draft to the call and take notes on any redline requests. Karthik/Monica: prepare the SOC coverage mapping and a short bullets doc on control coverage for production inference (encryption, access controls, logging, BC/DR).

Laura Bennett
